dial.summary: Six of eight macro indicators are now supportive — the 2s10s yield curve upgraded from neutral to supportive on a confirmed 7bps 4-week steepening (+0.35% → +0.42%), Global M2 expanded to $103.2T, ISM Manufacturing holds at a 4-year high of 55.6%, the Fed balance sheet is stable at $6.75T, stablecoin dominance continues its 30-day decline (14.3% → 13.3%), and BTC funding rates remain near zero; DXY at 99.93 holds in the neutral band, and real yields eased from their 2.47% peak to 2.40% while remaining the lone structural headwind; BTC dominance at 56.58% (TOTAL crypto $2.28T) keeps the accumulation thesis intact, with July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) the next regime-change catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC 4-bank tracker, MacroMicro) at $103.2T as of August 6, 2026 — up from the $102.7T June 2026 reported aggregate (+$0.5T as July central bank data is incorporated); US M2 (H.6 weekly) rose +5.6% YoY to $23.16T in June 2026 (28th consecutive monthly increase); global aggregate YoY growth rate stable at ~5–6% with no contracting headwind; 4-week trend up: ~$102.5T (early July estimate) → $103.2T (Aug 6) = +$0.7T / +0.68%, above the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY growth remains positive; headwind condition — contracting YoY — not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3, 2026) remains the most recent reading — 2.3pp above June's 53.3%, highest since May 2022, seventh consecutive expansion month; August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI does not release until September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%, Employment 52.8% (first factory expansion in 33 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; companion ISM Services PMI 54.1% (Aug 5); July NFP released August 7 at 8:30 AM ET — conflicting labor signals (ISM Mfg Employment 52.8% bullish vs ISM Services Employment 47.4% bearish, first contraction since June 2024); 4-week trend up: 53.3% (June) → 55.6% (July) = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.93 on August 7, 2026 pre-NFP (up 0.09% from August 6's close; intraday range 99.57–99.97); DXY rebounded from the August 4 Asian-session low of 99.29 to above 99.9 as markets repriced ahead of July NFP (consensus 83–97.5k vs June's 57k); the week of August 3–7 was the worst for DXY in three months (prior week closed near 100.3, gapping down to 99.29 on Monday); 30-day trend: ~101.34 (July 1) → 99.93 (Aug 7) = –1.4%, above the 0.5% flat threshold, trend down; status NEUTRAL per ICE DXY spot threshold (99.93 is above the 97.5 supportive boundary but below the 100 headwind boundary); July CPI (Aug 12) is the primary directional catalyst — sub-3% would pressure DXY toward 97.5 (supportive), a hot print would restore above 100 (headwind).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) at 2.40% as of August 4, 2026 (FRED H.15) — easing from the July 31 peak of 2.47% as nominal 10Y yields declined from 4.75% to 4.63% in the days following oil-driven disinflation; real yields have given back ~7bps from peak as pre-NFP positioning anticipates some labor softening; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 7 estimate) → 2.40% (Aug 4) = +22bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold; September FOMC cut probability constrained by ISM Manufacturing at 55.6%; July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) are the primary real-yield compression catalysts — DFII10 below 2.0% would flip status to neutral).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 4, 2026: DGS10 4.63%, DGS2 4.21%, spread +0.42% (+42bps); 4-week comparison: July 7 spread ~+0.35% (+35bps) → Aug 4 ~+0.42% (+42bps) = +7bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold — trend up; status upgraded from neutral to SUPPORTIVE (curve is positive at +42bps AND steepening on a 4-week basis exceeding the 5bps threshold); the 7bps steepening reflects markets pricing higher September FOMC cut probability driven by soft June NFP (57k) and ISM Services Employment contraction (47.4%); July NFP (Aug 7) and July CPI (Aug 12) are near-term curve catalysts — a weak print would compress the 2Y and steepen further; FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) and Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29) are the subsequent major catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL from H.4.1: $6,749M ($6.749T) for week ending August 5, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 6); up ~$11B from the July 29 reading ($6,738B), continuing minimal sequential change consistent with near-zero QT pace; 4-week trend flat: ~$6,720B (July 8 estimate) → $6,749B (Aug 5) = +$29B (+0.43%), just within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 plateau; roughly $95B above one year ago; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates; the July 29 FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% in a 9-3 vote — the most divided since 2016, with three dissents for a cut — suggesting the balance sheet normalization pace remains slow).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Live funding rate data inaccessible — CoinGlass returned network-blocked error; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; contextual signals as of August 7, 2026: BTC dominance 56.58%, BTC market cap $1.29T, total crypto market cap $2.28T; macro backdrop (ISM Manufacturing 55.6%, M2 $103.2T expanding, 2s10s now supportive) consistent with spot accumulation rather than leveraged long speculation; near-zero positive funding well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June toward near-zero); status supportive (near-zero funding signals healthy long bias without leverage overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $302B (USDT ~$188B, USDC ~$78B, balance in USDS/DAI/PYUSD) as of August 7, 2026; total crypto market cap $2.28T; stablecoin dominance $302B / $2.28T ≈ 13.28%; marginal tick from yesterday's 13.2% — essentially flat day-over-day as stablecoin issuance kept pace with TOTAL crypto; 30-day trend down: July 7 dominance ~14.3% → Aug 7 ~13.3% = –1.0pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; headwind threshold requires rising dominance WHILE TOTAL crypto is also rising — not met since dominance fell net over 30 days as TOTAL rose from ~$2.10T to $2.28T).

upcoming.title: Reserve Bank of Australia Rate Decision (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision at 14:30 AEST — first major central bank decision of the week; Fed is on hold at 3.50–3.75% (July 29 hold, 9-3 vote), BOE held at 3.75% (July 30); market watching for any global dovish pivot signals ahead of July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19); outcome influences commodity currencies (AUD/USD) and signals global growth durability, complementing the ISM Manufacturing 55.6% expansion narrative.

upcoming.title: CPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the most important inflation print ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC; arrives five days after July NFP; real yields at 2.40% (headwind) and DXY at 99.93 (neutral) make a soft CPI the primary catalyst for real-yield compression and a potential DXY break below 97.5 (which would flip DXY to supportive); ISM Prices Paid elevated in both Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services (above 70 in July), signaling pipeline cost pressure; however the oil-price decline on Iran diplomatic news provides a deflationary offset in the energy CPI component; June core PCE came in soft at 0.1% MoM; a hot July CPI risks pushing DXY back above 100 (restoring headwind) and is the principal near-term risk to the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: PPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released one day after July CPI (August 12); PPI feeds directly into core PCE components (healthcare and financial services); ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 71.1% in July signals upstream pipeline pressure, but the oil price decline on Iran news may provide a significant goods PPI offset; a soft PPI following a soft CPI would reinforce disinflation and support real-yield compression from 2.40% heading into the September FOMC; a hot PPI — especially in trade services or healthcare — would signal pipeline inflation risks not captured in headline CPI, complicating September cut pricing and potentially pushing DXY back above 100.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ending August 8, 2026 — first labor market read following the July NFP (August 7); prior weeks have shown low claims (~197–225k); ISM Services Employment contracted to 47.4% in July (first contraction since June 2024), raising downside risk to claims; released alongside July PPI; continuing claims also closely watched for signs of labor market softening ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — key consumption gauge released one week after July NFP and two days after CPI; June 2026 retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, +6.7% YoY; ISM Manufacturing at 55.6% (Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%) and ISM Services Business Activity at 59.1% suggest demand-side support; a strong retail print (>0.4% MoM) would confirm soft-landing narrative and reinforce BTC Accumulation; a miss alongside weak NFP would compound September cut signals and put real yields on a compression path.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released alongside July Retail Sales; July 2026 UMich sentiment: 54.4 (highest since February 2026, beating 51.0 estimate); August preliminary is the first consumer confidence read post-July NFP (Aug 7) and post-July CPI (Aug 12), capturing near-term inflation expectations; the 5-year inflation expectation component is particularly watched given ISM Prices Paid elevated in both Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services (above 70); oil-price decline on Iran diplomatic news may reduce 1-year inflation expectations and lift the headline sentiment reading.
